newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals up, gold posts strong gains.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals up, gold posts strong gains.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures ended higher on Tuesday, buoyed by the yen's fall against the dollar and stronger bullion prices, traders said.
Gold prices posted robust gains. They ranged from 10 yen to 15 yen per gram higher. Most-active benchmark February was up 15 yen at 1,410 yen.

"Active short-covering by overseas investors boosted bullion prices in the afternoon, and reflecting this, trade houses were forced to cover their short positions while private investors built fresh longs upon seeing the yen's fall," a trading house trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $362.50/80 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $361.70/362.20 in New York on Monday.
The trader said the TOCOM February gold is likely to test 1,420 yen per gram in the near-future, as gold prices have lagged behind sharp gains in the platinum group metals.
Platinum and palladium futures settled mostly higher, but off early highs amid caution that prices were too high, the traders said.
Most palladium futures marked all-time highs in early Tokyo trade. Benchmark February palladium ended up one yen per gram at 573 yen.

Trading in palladium futures was nervous. Uncertainty over the Russian metal supplies, along with a possibity that Russian export agency will soon inform Japanese traders of the timing of the export talks, made local investors edgy.

"Caution that palladium prices were too high prompted private investors to sell the metal after most prices hit all-time highs in early Tokyo trade," one trader said. "But constant physical buying supported prices," he said.
Platinum futures moved in line with palladium. Benchmark February platinum was up one yen at 1,491 yen. Benchmark February silver was up 1.7 yen per 10 grams at 208.2 yen.
